blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
World Action Models (WAMs) couple action generation with future visual prediction for robotic manipulation.
However, completing the joint video-action denoising process at each replanning cycle incurs substantial latency, delaying action updates and limiting closed-loop responsiveness.
We present Rolling-WAM, a formulation that distributes joint denoising across successive replanning cycles.
Our method maintains a sliding window of video-action chunks at staggered noise levels.
At each step, a rolling noise schedule fully denoises the imminent action chunk for execution,
while partially refining farther-future chunks.
As the window advances with new camera observations, the retained future chunks continue their denoising process.
This distributes the computational cost over time while carrying an evolving visual-action context across chunk boundaries.
Evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world Unitree G1 humanoid show that Rolling-WAM achieves competitive manipulation performance.
By removing the need to denoise the entire prediction horizon from scratch, it delivers a 4.5 × 4.5\times steady-state replanning speedup over standard joint WAMs.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
World Action Models (WAMs) have recently advanced robotic
manipulation by jointly predicting robot actions and future
observations [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] .
This joint modeling provides visual context for action
generation, helping the policy anticipate how the scene
will evolve.
However, deployment in dynamic environments requires
closed-loop control: the robot must repeatedly replan from
the latest observations to correct execution errors and
respond to environmental changes.

We argue that denoising can be organized more efficiently
across replanning cycles.
Conventional chunk-based samplers [ 2 , 4 ] fully denoise a new prediction horizon at each replan,
even when receding-horizon control executes only an
initial portion.
The unexecuted tail can inform current actions but is
discarded rather than reused across replans.
Retaining and progressively refining future video–action
chunks across cycles can preserve predictive context and
reuse denoising computation, reducing the sequential steps
needed to produce the next executable chunk.

We therefore introduce Rolling-WAM, a formulation that
inherits this intuition by distributing denoising across
successive replanning cycles.
Building on the concept of rolling diffusion for sequence

This resembles the intuition behind human planning:
near-term actions are concrete, while more distant plans
remain provisional and are refined as new observations arrive.

blocks.en:
We evaluate Rolling-WAM on simulation benchmarks, including LIBERO [ 7 ] and RoboTwin [ 8 ] , as well as three real-world humanoid manipulation tasks on the Unitree G1.
Our experiments demonstrate that Rolling-WAM retains the benefits of visual imagination while significantly reducing computational overhead.
It achieves a 98.1% average success rate on LIBERO and 93.3% on RoboTwin, remaining competitive with or exceeding state-of-the-art WAMs.

我们的实验表明,Rolling-WAM保留了视觉想象的好处,同时大大减少了计算间接费用.
它在LIBERO取得了98.1%的平均成功率,在RoboTwin实现了93.3%的平均成功率,保持了与最先进的WAM的竞争力或超过最先进的WAM.

blocks.en:
Our primary contribution is a rolling formulation for joint video-action models that distributes denoising across successive replanning cycles.
We demonstrate that this formulation achieves a 4.5 × 4.5\times inference speedup over standard WAMs while maintaining competitive manipulation performance.

我们证明,这种提法在保持竞争性操纵性能的同时,比标准WAM加快了4.5×4.5\的推论速度.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A World Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
blocks.zh: II-A 机器人操纵世界行动模式

blocks.en:
World Action Models (WAMs) augment action generation with future visual prediction.
Early approaches infer actions from language-conditioned video plans [ 9 ] .
Recent methods integrate visual prediction and action generation using pretrained video models [ 1 , 2 , 10 ] , often incorporating multimodal understanding [ 11 , 3 ] or exploring native causal video-action pretraining [ 12 ] .
Alternative designs learn predictive latent representations for action generation to avoid iterative future-video denoising at deployment [ 13 , 14 ] .
For joint WAMs, however, iterative video-action denoising remains computationally costly, motivating more efficient model designs and sampling strategies.
blocks.zh:
世界行动模式(WAMS)通过未来视觉预测增强行动生成能力。
早期方法从语言条件的视频计划中推断出行动[9].
近期的方法利用预先训练的视频模型[1, 2, 10]整合了视觉预测和动作生成,经常包含多模式理解[11, 3]或探索本土因果视频动作预训[12].
替代设计为行动生成学习预测性潜在表示,以避免在部署时重复使用未来视频代号[13、14]。
然而,对于联合的WAM来说,迭代视频动作解吸仍然具有计算成本,激励更有效的模型设计和取样战略。

blocks.en: II-B Efficient Inference for World Action Models
blocks.zh: II-B 世界行动模式的有效推论

blocks.en:
Accelerating WAM inference typically involves reducing the computational burden of future prediction.
Some methods remove future-video generation entirely at deployment [ 4 ] or extract future context in a single video-expert pass to cache for action denoising [ 15 ] .
Other architectural optimizations include reducing model size, visual tokens, and video denoising steps [ 16 ] , or accelerating sampling through modality-aware consistency distillation [ 17 ] .
Other strategies focus on context reuse, either by recycling visual features after partial joint denoising [ 18 ] or by sharing asynchronously refreshed visual context across action updates [ 19 ] .
Complementarily, real-time chunking overlaps inference with execution and uses action inpainting to align successive chunks [ 20 ] .
Instead of removing or caching future predictions, Rolling-WAM distributes the joint video-action denoising process across replanning cycles, progressively refining near-term and future predictions within a sliding window.
blocks.zh:
加速WAM推论通常涉及减少未来预测的计算负担.
一些方法在部署[4]时完全删除未来-视频生成,或者在单个视频-专家通行证中提取未来上下文,以缓存动作解析[15].
其他建筑优化包括缩小模型尺寸,视觉符号,以及视频解码步骤[16],或者通过模式-意识一致性蒸馏[17]加速采样.
其他战略侧重于背景再利用,要么在部分联合点名[18]后回收视觉特征,要么在整个行动更新中共享同步更新的视觉环境[19]。
作为补充,实时划分与执行的推论重叠,并使用动作涂片来对接连续的块[20].
Rolling-WAM没有删除或缓存未来的预测,而是在整个重新规划周期中分发联合视频动作解禁过程,在滑动窗口内逐步完善近期和未来预测.

blocks.en: II-C Rolling Diffusion for Sequence Generation
blocks.zh: II-C 为序列生成而滚动扩散

blocks.en:
Rolling Diffusion [ 5 ] introduces a sliding denoising window with progressively higher noise levels toward the future.
This concept has been extended with independent token noise levels for flexible sampling schedules [ 21 ] and bidirectional denoising with rollout-based distillation for autoregressive long-video generation [ 6 ] .
These works motivate the rolling formulation of Rolling-WAM.
blocks.zh:
滚动扩散[5]引入了滑动的消音窗口,未来噪音水平逐渐提高.
这一概念得到了扩展,为灵活的采样时间表提供了独立的信号噪声水平[21],为自动回转长视频生成提供了以推出为基础的蒸馏法双向去诺[6]。
这些作品推动了滚滚式WAM的滚动配制.

blocks.en:
In robotic manipulation, Streaming Diffusion Policy [ 22 ] and RNR-DP [ 23 ] maintain partially denoised action buffers to accelerate action generation.
However, these methods focus exclusively on action-only denoising and evaluate on task-specific policies in relatively small-scale settings.
We extend this rolling mechanism to couple world modeling with action generation, enabling action tokens to attend to partially denoised visual futures, and evaluate our approach across broader multitask settings.
blocks.zh:
在机器人操纵中,流传扩散政策[22]和RNR-DP[23]保持了部分去通知的动作缓冲器,以加速动作生成.
然而,这些方法完全侧重于在相对小规模的环境中,仅以行动为目的对特定任务的政策进行发号施令和评估。
我们把这一滚动机制推广到与行动生成的对等世界模式,使行动标志能够关注部分被淡化的视觉未来,并评估我们在整个多任务环境中的做法。

blocks.en: III Method
blocks.zh: 三、结 论 方法

blocks.en:
This section presents Rolling-WAM, a joint video-action model for low-latency closed-loop robotic control.
We first formulate the visual-action modeling problem and identify the computational bottleneck of standard joint denoising (Sec. III-A ).
We then introduce a rolling denoising mechanism that maintains a sliding window of predictions at staggered noise levels (Sec. III-B ).
Next, we describe the sampling and execution process that distributes computation across control cycles (Sec. III-C ).
Finally, we detail the model architecture and the training objective (Sec. III-D ).
blocks.zh:
本节介绍Rolling-WAM,低纬度闭路机器人控制的联合视频动作模型.
我们首先制定视觉动作模型问题,并找出标准联合解析(Sec. III-A.)的计算瓶颈。
然后,我们采用滚动调试机制,在交错噪音水平上维持一个预测的滑动窗口(Sec.III-B)。
其次,我们描述在整个控制周期中分配计算(第III-C节)的取样和执行过程。
最后,我们详细介绍了示范架构和培训目标(第III-D节)。

blocks.en:
Deploying WAMs in a closed loop requires multiple denoising steps within each replanning cycle before an action chunk is executed.
This iterative process incurs a high computational cost.
It increases inference latency and limits the responsiveness of the controller to new observations.

这种迭代过程的计算成本很高.
它增加了推论延迟性,限制了控制者对新观测的反应.

blocks.en:
As shown in Fig. 2 , Rolling-WAM addresses this bottleneck by distributing the denoising computation across successive replanning cycles.
It maintains a sliding window that jointly refines the next action chunk and its future continuation.
This approach completes near-term predictions while leaving longer-term chunks partially denoised at staggered noise levels.
As the window advances with execution, the retained predictions continue to evolve under new observations.
This mechanism carries predictive context across chunk boundaries, allowing successive action chunks to be generated with a shared, evolving visual-action future.

它维持一个滑动窗口,共同完善下一个行动块及其未来的延续。
这种方法完成近期预测,同时将长期块部分去除交错噪音水平。
随着窗口随着执行的推进,保留预测在新的观察下继续演变.
这种机制具有跨块边界的预测性背景,使得连续的动作块能够随着共同的、不断发展的视觉动作未来而产生.

Each chunk traverses all N N denoising steps before execution, but its computation is distributed across multiple replanning cycles.

blocks.en:
As shown in Fig. 2 (a), Rolling-WAM pairs a pretrained video Diffusion Transformer [ 24 , 25 ] with a lightweight action Transformer in a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture [ 4 , 26 ] .
The video expert processes VAE latents of the current observation and noisy future video.
The action expert processes projected noisy actions.
Masked joint attention couples the experts at each layer, allowing action generation to draw on pretrained visual dynamics.
Language and proprioceptive embeddings condition both experts through cross-attention.

The attention mask (Fig. 2 c) allows every action chunk to attend to visual features across the entire prediction window.
Direct action-to-action attention is restricted to the same chunk, and video tokens do not attend to action tokens.
Each action chunk therefore draws on a shared, evolving visual prediction that extends beyond its own execution interval.

blocks.en:
Our experiments verify whether rolling denoising can accelerate joint video-action prediction while preserving manipulation performance.
We compare task success with a broad set of vision-language-action models and world action models on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world Unitree G1 tasks.
Controlled latency measurements quantify the computational savings of rolling denoising.
Ablations examine the roles of window size, training noise schedules, and cross-chunk action attention.

blocks.en: V Conclusion
blocks.zh: 五 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we presented Rolling-WAM, an efficient World
Action Model that jointly refines near-term and future
video-action predictions within a sliding window.
By distributing denoising across replanning cycles, it
reduces the sequential steps needed to produce the next
executable action chunk, while using partially denoised
visual futures to guide action generation.
Experiments show that Rolling-WAM achieves competitive
performance on LIBERO and outperforms the compared methods
on RoboTwin 2.0 and real-world humanoid manipulation tasks, while delivering substantial speedups in inference over standard joint WAMs.
Combining rolling denoising with complementary model and
system optimizations offers further opportunities for
low-latency robot control.
